section_summary: This section contains diplomatic despatches, cross-reference sheets, and a telegram from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo dating from June 1930 to February 1932 regarding the personnel and organization of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Gaimusho) and its diplomatic and consular missions worldwide. Despatches No. 186 (June 1930), No. 459 (March 1931), and No. 482 (February 1932) transmit detailed official rosters of Japanese Foreign Office officials arranged both by departmental posting and by imperial civil service seniority. Interspersed cross-reference sheets and Telegram No. 7 document diplomatic transfers and political developments, including the assumption of office by Foreign Minister Kenkichi Yoshizawa in January 1932 amidst escalating Far Eastern tensions.

subfiles.about: Transmits comprehensive lists of officials in the Japanese Foreign Office and Foreign Service arranged by departmental assignment and seniority rank.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 186 from Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Tokyo, transmitting to the Secretary of State two enclosed personnel rosters of the Japanese diplomatic and consular service dated June 13, 1930. Enclosure 1 details the organization of the Foreign Office in Tokyo—including the Minister's secretariat, bureaus of protocol and personnel, correspondence and records, accounts, translation, telegrams, Asiatic affairs, European and American affairs, commercial affairs, treaties, information and intelligence, and cultural enterprises—followed by embassies, legations, and consulates worldwide. Enclosure 2 ranks all Foreign Office personnel according to imperial civil service status, from Shinnin and Chokunin ranks down through the Sixth Grade of the Higher Civil Service.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 186 transmitting Lists of Japanese Foreign Office Officials and Foreign Service Officers

subfiles.about: Records diplomatic and Foreign Office personnel reassignments reported in Tokyo Despatch No. 38 of November 4, 1930.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Document File Note on Despatch No. 38: Foreign Office changes, including Hirota to Moscow, Arita to Austria, Shiratori Information Bureau chief and Obata to Germany.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Foreign Office Personnel Changes (Despatch No. 38)

subfiles.about: Transmits updated official rosters of the Japanese Foreign Office and Foreign Service as of February 9, 1931, organized by post and by civil service seniority.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 459 from Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Tokyo, transmitting to the Secretary of State updated rosters of Japanese Foreign Office personnel and diplomatic/consular officers as of February 9, 1931. Enclosure 1 provides an exhaustive organizational breakdown of the Foreign Office ministries, bureaus, sections, overseas embassies, legations, and consulates. Enclosure 2 arranges all officers by official seniority rank from imperial Shinnin rank through Seventh Grade of the Higher Civil Service, capturing the reassignments following the late 1930 diplomatic shuffle.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 459 transmitting Lists of Japanese Foreign Office Officials and Foreign Service Officers

subfiles.about: Cross-references Tokyo Telegram No. 7 regarding Kenkichi Yoshizawa assuming office as Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 7 (January 14, 1932; 793.94/3512): Yoshizawa takes office as Foreign Minister.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Foreign Minister Yoshizawa Taking Office (Telegram No. 7)

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese public reaction to the American note of January 7, Yoshizawa assuming the post of Foreign Minister, and a naval landing incident at Tsingtao.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Forbes reports no knowledge of a Japanese blockade plan, the January 7 American note was accepted calmly, Yoshizawa takes office that evening, and 300 bluejackets landed then left Tsingtao.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7 from Tokyo regarding Yoshizawa Taking Office and Far Eastern Situation

subfiles.about: Cross-references Despatch No. 482 of February 6, 1932, transmitting lists of Japanese Foreign Office officials.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 482 (February 6, 1932) sending updated rosters of Japanese Foreign Office officials (701.9400 Diplomatic List/2).
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 482 Transmitting List of Foreign Office Officials

subfiles.about: Transmits updated personnel rosters of the Japanese Foreign Office and Foreign Service as of January 20, 1932, categorized by department and by civil service seniority.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Embassy, Tokyo, Japan
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 482 from Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes in Tokyo transmitting to the Secretary of State updated personnel rosters of the Japanese Foreign Office and Foreign Service dated January 20, 1932. Enclosure 1 details the departmental organization under new Foreign Minister Kenkichi Yoshizawa, Parliamentary Vice Minister Viscount Takanori Iwaki, Vice Minister Matsuzo Nagai, and Parliamentary Councillor Bumajiro Takahashi, including embassies, legations, and consulates. Enclosure 2 arranges diplomatic and consular personnel in order of imperial civil service seniority from Shinnin rank down through Higher Civil Service Fifth Grade, with the remaining grades continuing beyond page 80.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 482 transmitting Lists of Japanese Foreign Office Officials and Foreign Service Officers
